Title: Norfolk Southern CEO: we're in a 'manufacturing super-cycle'
Text: ['"We\'ve got the most powerful automotive franchise in the east, and so it\'s only a matter of time when that recovers", says Alan Shaw, President and CEO of Norfolk Southern (NSC). He spoke with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi about the current downturn in the rail industry. Shaw attributed the decline to broader economic factors, like the freight recession in the trucking market, which has suppressed spot market rates and inventory restocking.', 'Despite these headwinds, Shaw expressed confidence that the rail industry is entering a "manufacturing super-cycle."', 'When the U.S. consumer and the truck market recovers, we\'re gonna be "coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals", Shaw told Yahoo Finance.', 'Click here to watch more from Yahoo Finance Invest.', 'BRIAN SOZZI: A lot of focus so far at the conference on the state of the economy, heard Hans Vestberg, the chairman and CEO of Verizon talked about the consumer is doing well, the lodging industry, Marriott CEO, Anthony Capuano talking about that doing well but maybe just a little bit of a slowdown. The rail industry is in a down cycle. Why?', 'ALAN SHAW: What industry did you say?', 'BRIAN SOZZI: The rail industry is--', "ALAN SHAW: You know, what we're seeing is a really weak truck market, overcapacity in trucking, and so there's been kind of a freight recession in the truck market for about 22 months. There's some indication that that's ending, right? Spot markets are no longer on the decline. As I talk to customers, we're seeing inventory destocking come to an end. And as-- we serve 5,000 customers so we've got this really unique view of the US economy. We touch about every market.", "And as I look around, you're starting to see this consumer do fairly well as you noted, I believe we're in a manufacturing supercycle. We've seen investment in new factory builds triple and-- so far in 2023 relative to they were-- the run rate they were in the previous decade, and it's really in our service region, it's in the Midwest, and it's in the Southeast.", "And I was talking to the CEO of a European automaker and he was talking about how if he wants to sell production in the United States, he needs to produce in the United States and there's a lot of advantages for onshoring and-- in the United States and it's cheap and reliable electricity, it's a logistics infrastructure that's already in place, and it's a talented workforce and that really plays to the strengths of our strategy going forward, which is to use service to drive top tier revenue growth and industry competitive margins.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Important distinction there. So you're saying rail has been in a down cycle, but that's not the same as a recession?", "ALAN SHAW: No, I don't-- I don't believe we're in a recession. I think we're in a-- we've been in a freight recession, because there's been overcapacity in the truck market and that's our primary form of competition. Now we've got the most powerful intermodal franchise in the East, and so it's only a matter of time when that recovers and when the US consumer does recover and the truck market can-- recovers, we're going to be coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals."]

Title: How Norfolk Southern is changing after train derailment
Text: ["Norfolk Southern (NSC) has been under a microscope ever since the major chemical spill in East Palestine, Ohio. The company has taken major steps toward addressing safety concerns, including new training programs. Alan Shaw, Norfolk Southern CEO and President, sits down with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to discuss the company's progress with the ongoing cleanup in East Palestine as well as the strides the company is making in safety.", 'Shaw explains efforts made to improve safety. "We have... a machine visioning train inspection portal, which is basically a shed that goes around the tracks, train goes through track speed about 60 miles an hour. It\'s got 38 cameras that take about a thousand pictures of each rail car and immediately uses AI to spot potential safety defects...What we are focused on at Norfolk Southern is enhancing safety and enhancing service and really competing in that $860 billion dollar truck and logistics market."', 'Click here to watch more from Yahoo Finance Invest.', "BRIAN SOZZI: I know it's been an incredibly busy time for your company, and I was thinking back like, how do you prepare for a segment like this? And I think it starts with understanding you as a human, as a leader. Of course, the train derailments are very much covered throughout news in East Palestine. Take us through how you were raised, your family upbringing, and-- because I think that tells a lot on how you respond to the situation.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah. I was-- my father was in Vietnam. He's a Marine Lieutenant, did two tours, and I was raised, for a number of years, by my grandmother, my aunt and my mom. Three really strong willed women. And my grandmother worked as an assistant in the financial aid office and put four kids through college, right.", "And she paid it forward, and she kept her promises, and that's one of the things I learned is trust, accountability and keeping your promises, and that's kind of the North Star and that's what we followed as we went through this crisis is we said we were going to make it right, we said we were going to do the right things, and each and every day we've kept our promises.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: When you get that call that a train derailed in East Palestine, toxic chemicals going into the air, who is Alan Shaw one minute after that call?', "ALAN SHAW: Oh, I'm thinking about the community. I'm thinking about the safety of our crews. I'm thinking about the safety of the first responders. Your immediate question is, any injuries, any deaths, any hazmat releases, and we're really fortunate that there were no injuries or deaths. I pulled the team together immediately afterwards, and I said, look, we're going to make this right. We're going to do the right thing.", "And I didn't know what that meant, right. I've never been to East Palace, and it's a wonderful community of about 4,700 people, but what I knew is I had to listen, I had to learn, I had to act with humility, and I had to take decisive action. And so I would go to the community. I've been there multiple times a month. I was just-- I was there just last week and you engage with the community and you go into listening sessions and you go into the churches and in the schools and in the family rooms and into the businesses and you ask them, what can Norfolk Southern do to help?", "I knew that we would bring Norfolk Southern's resources-- we're a strong company-- to bear and the community would direct where we'd go. And so we've already committed over $100 million to helping the community recover and helping the community thrive, and there's more work to be done.", "BRIAN SOZZI: As a leader, public company forward or the face of the company in many respects, what is it like to take that criticism that you've gotten even despite all the efforts you've been trying to put forth on the ground?", "ALAN SHAW: We're a safe railroad, and I knew that. Last year, the number of derailments on Norfolk Southern was the lowest in two decades. But I know we can get better. And as I looked through this crisis-- a crisis is an opportunity to really kind of like test your leadership and your resolve, it also is an opportunity to accelerate change.", 'And I knew that coming out of this, we were going to be a stronger company. And so one of the things I did is I looked outside the rail industry for inspiration. I used to work at Newport News Shipbuilding in the nuclear department installing nuclear reactors and aircraft carriers, and so I had a really good idea--', "BRIAN SOZZI: That's a pressure cooker.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah. I had a really good idea of the safety culture of the Admiral Rickover's nuclear Navy, and so I reached out to a former Admiral who used to run the Navy nuclear propulsion system and asked him to put together a team of former Navy nukes reporting directly to me as an independent consultant and help us with our safety culture. And they've been on the ground for about six months.", "They're going to be here two to three years. They're engaging with our employees, our craft colleagues, and they're going to make us a safer railroad. We're going to be the gold standard of safety.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: So three years from now, how do you-- how is Norfolk a safer railroad?', "ALAN SHAW: Well, we're going to continue to invest in our infrastructure. We invest over $1 billion in safety every year. We're going to continue to train our employees. We're going to use technology. We have partnered with the Georgia Tech Research Institute on a machine visioning train inspection portal, which is basically a shed that goes around the tracks.", "The train goes through it, track speed about 60 miles an hour. It's got 38 cameras that take about 1,000 pictures of each rail car and immediately uses AI to spot potential safety defects. And that's something that I know that a conductor in Chicago at night in February just won't catch with the human eye. We are using technology and automated intelligence to enhance our safety.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: What are some of the specifics that Norfolk is doing on the ground in East Palestine? And how are you putting the capital to work to rebuild the community?', "ALAN SHAW: So a number of things. We just achieved a pretty significant milestone just about a week or two ago as we exited the most intense phase of the environmental remediation. Brian, we moved 170,000 tons of contaminated soil off site to EPA approved landfills, which were specifically designed to handle that. We've moved 36 million gallons of contaminated water off site. So that's a big move for the community.", "We've announced a $20 million park improvement project. One of the first times I was there, I met with some community leaders in someone's basement, and they talked to me a lot about the park, and so I went to the park. It's an 81 acre facility in the middle of the community that's a source of pride for them, and they asked me if I could help them improve it, and so I brought Norfolk Southern's resources to bear.", "I was just at a groundbreaking ceremony a couple of weeks ago for a regional first responder training facility. We're committing $20 million to that, and that really-- that's important to me personally, because I wanted to express my appreciation for the first responders from Ohio and Pennsylvania and West Virginia who rushed to the scene. They're the heroes here. And first responders are folks who devote their entire career to protecting the communities we serve.", "BRIAN SOZZI: What do you think when you hear politicians say railroads are not safe, they're just trying to jack up their profits by taking away safety standards?", "ALAN SHAW: Well, railroads are clearly the safest form of transportation across land, we're also the most efficient. Now what we're focused on, on Norfolk Southern is enhancing safety and enhancing service and really competing in that $860 billion truck and logistics market, you know. We want to have top tier revenue growth in the industry with industry competitive margins, that's the strategy that we announced about seven months after I became CEO last year.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: There are a lot of lawsuits regarding this situation. Is there-- do you see an insight to them being settled in one fell swoop?', "ALAN SHAW: You know, I'm leaving that up to our legal team. There are a number of lawsuits, and I really can't comment on that. What I can tell you is we're going to continue to get better coming out of this. We're going to be a stronger company. We're advancing safety. We're advancing service. I'm really proud of the way that we've responded to this.", 'The entire organization has become aligned around our new strategy, our new vision and our response in East Palestine.', 'BRIAN SOZZI: Is it right that the total cost so far is-- I think it was it $966 million? Is that--', "ALAN SHAW: Yeah, we've estimated around $900 million so far. Now there could be additional lawsuits, there could be additional fines, there could also be insurance settlements. In fact, we've already started to pull those in. And there could be third party claims as well.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: So for an investor looking to put money to work in Norfolk Southern, is that-- should they expect a similar number? I imagine this weighs on the finances of the company. Is that number similar-- that might pop up next year in terms of total cost?', "ALAN SHAW: You know, much of that cost has been the environmental remediation. As I noted, we've exited the most intense phase of that but there are other things that could come up with lawsuits or fines but again, the insurance settlements as well.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: A lot of focus so far at the conference on the state of the economy. Heard Hans Vestberg, chairman and CEO of Verizon, talk about the consumer is doing well, the lodging industry, Marriott CEO, Anthony Capuano talking about that doing well but maybe just a little bit of a slowdown. The rail industry is in a down cycle. Why?', 'ALAN SHAW: What industry did you say?', 'BRIAN SOZZI: The rail industry.', "ALAN SHAW: You know, what we're seeing is a really weak truck market, overcapacity in trucking, and so there's been kind of a Great Recession in the truck market for about 22 months. There's some indication that that's ending, right? Spot markets are no longer on the decline as I talk to customers. We're seeing inventory destocking come to an end.", "And as-- we serve 5,000 customers so we've got this really unique view of the US economy. We touch about every market. And as I look around, you're starting to see this consumer do fairly well as you noted. I believe we're in a manufacturing supercycle. We've seen investment in new factory builds triple and so far in 2023 relative to they were-- the run rate they were in the previous decade, and it's really in our service region, it's in the Midwest, and it's in the Southeast.", "And I was talking to the CEO of a European automaker, and he was talking about how if he wants to sell production in the United States, he needs to produce in the United States, and there's a lot of advantages for onshoring and-- in the United States and it's cheap and reliable electricity, it's a logistics infrastructure that's already in place, and it's a talented workforce and that really plays to the strengths of our strategy going forward, which is to use service to drive top tier revenue growth and industry competitive margins.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Important distinction there. So you're saying rail has been in a down cycle, but that's not the same as a recession?", "ALAN SHAW: No, I don't-- I don't believe we're in a recession. I think we're in a-- we've been in a freight recession, because there's been overcapacity in the truck market and that's our primary form of competition. Now we've got the most powerful intermodal franchise in the East, and so it's only a matter of time when that recovers.", "And when the US consumer does recover and the truck market recovers, we're going to be coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: Have you had to furlough any workers?', "ALAN SHAW: No, we continue to hire, right. We're building for the long-term at Norfolk Southern. We're investing in our future and we're investing in locomotives and intermodal facilities and freight cars that help us compete with truck and technology and safety and our people as well. That's been my commitment. And day one that I became CEO about 18 months ago, I was out in the field, and I was visiting with our crews in the crew rooms and in the locomotive cabs, because I wanted to express my deep appreciation and respect for what they do for Norfolk Southern, for our customers and for the US economy.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Well, it's like you're still-- you work your whole life, Alan-- and I think a lot of people watching this can relate and a lot of probably a lot of people in this room. You work your whole life to get to this top spot and within 18 months, you're dealing with a major crisis. What has that like been-- been that for you personally? What has that been like?", "ALAN SHAW: As you-- the first day you sit in the seat, you understand it's about accountability, right, and I just knew that each and every day, we were going to do the next right thing. I was going to follow our North Star. I was going to follow our values, focus on the long-term, and my goal for my team is-- was that 5 years from now, 10 years from now, when we look back on this, we can have a response that makes us proud and a response that makes the folks in East Palestine proud.", "At the same time, we're implementing this unique vision, a better way forward in the rail industry. Look, if you think about rail, rail is seated sharing to truck for the last 25 years despite being lower cost, a higher safety, better much-- better safety metrics, better sustainability with respect to the carbon footprint, and it's because rail hasn't delivered consistently a good service product.", "And so when I became CEO about 18 months ago, we went on a hiring spree. We started hiring conductors. We're investing in the future and we're investing in service, because I've got so much confidence in the unique strengths of our franchise and our customers and our employees that I know that we can deliver that top tier revenue growth with industry competitive margins. That's what's going to drive long-term shareholder value for Norfolk Southern.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Lastly, Alan, we're about 15 seconds left. Throughout this crisis period, as a leader, how have you stayed centered? These have to be incredibly challenging periods.", "ALAN SHAW: I've got a lot of confidence that I know we're doing the right thing and so that allows you to block out a lot of-- a lot of the noise and focus on the mission. And when you get up every day, you just say each and every day, I'm going to do the next right thing, and I'm going to see this thing through.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Well, I look forward to continuing to track this progress. Norfolk Southern CEO, Alan Shaw. Thanks for coming down, and really, it's good to see you again. We appreciate it.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah, it's a pleasure, Brian. Thank you so much.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: Appreciate it.']

Title: 3 Dividend Stocks with Strong Growth Potential in Q4
Text: ['If this is the beginning of a broader market rally, many short-term investors may shift away from dividend stocks. After a year or more of playing defense, it makes\xa0sense that risk-tolerant traders and investors will want to consider equities with more upside. ', 'But, there’s still a case for solid dividend stocks in your portfolio. ', 'InvestorPlace - Stock Market News, Stock Advice & Trading Tips', 'And several of these companies are in line to raise their dividends during the next round of earnings. And sin stocks tend to perform well in bull or bear markets. Title: Shareholders in Norfolk Southern (NYSE:NSC) are in the red if they invested a year ago
Text: ['Passive investing in an index fund is a good way to ensure your own returns roughly match the overall market. Title: Cincinnati voters approve sale of city-owned railroad to Norfolk Southern
Text: ['Cincinnati voters decided on Election Day to allow their city to sell the Cincinnati Southern Railway to Norfolk Southern.', 'Tuesday’s vote was 51.56% in favor of the sale and 48.44% against the sale, according to Ballotpedia. By votes, those supporting the sale were 43,173 and those against the sale were 40,559 — a difference of 2,614.', 'The Cincinnati Southern Railway Board of Trustees owns the 382-mile railroad in a trust and leases it to NS (NYSE: NSC) for Cincinnati’s benefit. The city currently receives about $25 million annually from NS, according to a local news report in February.', 'The city announced in November 2022 that it was considering selling the railway to NS for $1.62 billion to help fund city infrastructure improvements, according to news reports. NS would pay for the transaction through a combination of internal and external sources, the railroad said last year.', 'Cincinnati has owned the land beneath the track for almost two centuries, but NS operates the rail line, according to NS.', 'In response to Tuesday’s note, NS spokesperson Tom Crosson said: “This is a victory for the citizens of Cincinnati. Current and future generations will reap the benefits of new infrastructure investments, helping to create a better future for the city. We appreciate all of the community leaders and groups who endorsed Issue 22 — especially Mayor Aftab Pureval, the City Council, and the Board of Trustees of the Cincinnati Southern Railway. We also thank the staff and volunteers who made this a successful campaign. Now, we will work with the city to finalize the sale, which we expect to close in Q1 of 2024.”', 'Subscribe to FreightWaves’ e-newsletters and get the latest insights on freight right in your inbox.', 'Click here for more FreightWaves articles by Joanna Marsh.', 'Cincinnati voters to decide on sale of Cincinnati Southern Railway to NS', 'Norfolk Southern wants close look at proposed CPKC-CSX Southeast corridor', 'Norfolk Southern says higher costs will pay off in long term', 'The post Cincinnati voters approve sale of city-owned railroad to Norfolk Southern appeared first on FreightWaves.']

Title: Norfolk Southern CEO: we're in a 'manufacturing super-cycle'
Text: ['"We\'ve got the most powerful automotive franchise in the east, and so it\'s only a matter of time when that recovers", says Alan Shaw, President and CEO of Norfolk Southern (NSC). He spoke with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi about the current downturn in the rail industry. Shaw attributed the decline to broader economic factors, like the freight recession in the trucking market, which has suppressed spot market rates and inventory restocking.', 'Despite these headwinds, Shaw expressed confidence that the rail industry is entering a "manufacturing super-cycle."', 'When the U.S. consumer and the truck market recovers, we\'re gonna be "coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals", Shaw told Yahoo Finance.', 'Click here to watch more from Yahoo Finance Invest.', 'BRIAN SOZZI: A lot of focus so far at the conference on the state of the economy, heard Hans Vestberg, the chairman and CEO of Verizon talked about the consumer is doing well, the lodging industry, Marriott CEO, Anthony Capuano talking about that doing well but maybe just a little bit of a slowdown. The rail industry is in a down cycle. Why?', 'ALAN SHAW: What industry did you say?', 'BRIAN SOZZI: The rail industry is--', "ALAN SHAW: You know, what we're seeing is a really weak truck market, overcapacity in trucking, and so there's been kind of a freight recession in the truck market for about 22 months. There's some indication that that's ending, right? Spot markets are no longer on the decline. As I talk to customers, we're seeing inventory destocking come to an end. And as-- we serve 5,000 customers so we've got this really unique view of the US economy. We touch about every market.", "And as I look around, you're starting to see this consumer do fairly well as you noted, I believe we're in a manufacturing supercycle. We've seen investment in new factory builds triple and-- so far in 2023 relative to they were-- the run rate they were in the previous decade, and it's really in our service region, it's in the Midwest, and it's in the Southeast.", "And I was talking to the CEO of a European automaker and he was talking about how if he wants to sell production in the United States, he needs to produce in the United States and there's a lot of advantages for onshoring and-- in the United States and it's cheap and reliable electricity, it's a logistics infrastructure that's already in place, and it's a talented workforce and that really plays to the strengths of our strategy going forward, which is to use service to drive top tier revenue growth and industry competitive margins.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Important distinction there. So you're saying rail has been in a down cycle, but that's not the same as a recession?", "ALAN SHAW: No, I don't-- I don't believe we're in a recession. I think we're in a-- we've been in a freight recession, because there's been overcapacity in the truck market and that's our primary form of competition. Now we've got the most powerful intermodal franchise in the East, and so it's only a matter of time when that recovers and when the US consumer does recover and the truck market can-- recovers, we're going to be coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals."]

Title: How Norfolk Southern is changing after train derailment
Text: ["Norfolk Southern (NSC) has been under a microscope ever since the major chemical spill in East Palestine, Ohio. The company has taken major steps toward addressing safety concerns, including new training programs. Alan Shaw, Norfolk Southern CEO and President, sits down with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to discuss the company's progress with the ongoing cleanup in East Palestine as well as the strides the company is making in safety.", 'Shaw explains efforts made to improve safety. "We have... a machine visioning train inspection portal, which is basically a shed that goes around the tracks, train goes through track speed about 60 miles an hour. It\'s got 38 cameras that take about a thousand pictures of each rail car and immediately uses AI to spot potential safety defects...What we are focused on at Norfolk Southern is enhancing safety and enhancing service and really competing in that $860 billion dollar truck and logistics market."', 'Click here to watch more from Yahoo Finance Invest.', "BRIAN SOZZI: I know it's been an incredibly busy time for your company, and I was thinking back like, how do you prepare for a segment like this? And I think it starts with understanding you as a human, as a leader. Of course, the train derailments are very much covered throughout news in East Palestine. Take us through how you were raised, your family upbringing, and-- because I think that tells a lot on how you respond to the situation.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah. I was-- my father was in Vietnam. He's a Marine Lieutenant, did two tours, and I was raised, for a number of years, by my grandmother, my aunt and my mom. Three really strong willed women. And my grandmother worked as an assistant in the financial aid office and put four kids through college, right.", "And she paid it forward, and she kept her promises, and that's one of the things I learned is trust, accountability and keeping your promises, and that's kind of the North Star and that's what we followed as we went through this crisis is we said we were going to make it right, we said we were going to do the right things, and each and every day we've kept our promises.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: When you get that call that a train derailed in East Palestine, toxic chemicals going into the air, who is Alan Shaw one minute after that call?', "ALAN SHAW: Oh, I'm thinking about the community. I'm thinking about the safety of our crews. I'm thinking about the safety of the first responders. Your immediate question is, any injuries, any deaths, any hazmat releases, and we're really fortunate that there were no injuries or deaths. I pulled the team together immediately afterwards, and I said, look, we're going to make this right. We're going to do the right thing.", "And I didn't know what that meant, right. I've never been to East Palace, and it's a wonderful community of about 4,700 people, but what I knew is I had to listen, I had to learn, I had to act with humility, and I had to take decisive action. And so I would go to the community. I've been there multiple times a month. I was just-- I was there just last week and you engage with the community and you go into listening sessions and you go into the churches and in the schools and in the family rooms and into the businesses and you ask them, what can Norfolk Southern do to help?", "I knew that we would bring Norfolk Southern's resources-- we're a strong company-- to bear and the community would direct where we'd go. And so we've already committed over $100 million to helping the community recover and helping the community thrive, and there's more work to be done.", "BRIAN SOZZI: As a leader, public company forward or the face of the company in many respects, what is it like to take that criticism that you've gotten even despite all the efforts you've been trying to put forth on the ground?", "ALAN SHAW: We're a safe railroad, and I knew that. Last year, the number of derailments on Norfolk Southern was the lowest in two decades. But I know we can get better. And as I looked through this crisis-- a crisis is an opportunity to really kind of like test your leadership and your resolve, it also is an opportunity to accelerate change.", 'And I knew that coming out of this, we were going to be a stronger company. And so one of the things I did is I looked outside the rail industry for inspiration. I used to work at Newport News Shipbuilding in the nuclear department installing nuclear reactors and aircraft carriers, and so I had a really good idea--', "BRIAN SOZZI: That's a pressure cooker.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah. I had a really good idea of the safety culture of the Admiral Rickover's nuclear Navy, and so I reached out to a former Admiral who used to run the Navy nuclear propulsion system and asked him to put together a team of former Navy nukes reporting directly to me as an independent consultant and help us with our safety culture. And they've been on the ground for about six months.", "They're going to be here two to three years. They're engaging with our employees, our craft colleagues, and they're going to make us a safer railroad. We're going to be the gold standard of safety.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: So three years from now, how do you-- how is Norfolk a safer railroad?', "ALAN SHAW: Well, we're going to continue to invest in our infrastructure. We invest over $1 billion in safety every year. We're going to continue to train our employees. We're going to use technology. We have partnered with the Georgia Tech Research Institute on a machine visioning train inspection portal, which is basically a shed that goes around the tracks.", "The train goes through it, track speed about 60 miles an hour. It's got 38 cameras that take about 1,000 pictures of each rail car and immediately uses AI to spot potential safety defects. And that's something that I know that a conductor in Chicago at night in February just won't catch with the human eye. We are using technology and automated intelligence to enhance our safety.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: What are some of the specifics that Norfolk is doing on the ground in East Palestine? And how are you putting the capital to work to rebuild the community?', "ALAN SHAW: So a number of things. We just achieved a pretty significant milestone just about a week or two ago as we exited the most intense phase of the environmental remediation. Brian, we moved 170,000 tons of contaminated soil off site to EPA approved landfills, which were specifically designed to handle that. We've moved 36 million gallons of contaminated water off site. So that's a big move for the community.", "We've announced a $20 million park improvement project. One of the first times I was there, I met with some community leaders in someone's basement, and they talked to me a lot about the park, and so I went to the park. It's an 81 acre facility in the middle of the community that's a source of pride for them, and they asked me if I could help them improve it, and so I brought Norfolk Southern's resources to bear.", "I was just at a groundbreaking ceremony a couple of weeks ago for a regional first responder training facility. We're committing $20 million to that, and that really-- that's important to me personally, because I wanted to express my appreciation for the first responders from Ohio and Pennsylvania and West Virginia who rushed to the scene. They're the heroes here. And first responders are folks who devote their entire career to protecting the communities we serve.", "BRIAN SOZZI: What do you think when you hear politicians say railroads are not safe, they're just trying to jack up their profits by taking away safety standards?", "ALAN SHAW: Well, railroads are clearly the safest form of transportation across land, we're also the most efficient. Now what we're focused on, on Norfolk Southern is enhancing safety and enhancing service and really competing in that $860 billion truck and logistics market, you know. We want to have top tier revenue growth in the industry with industry competitive margins, that's the strategy that we announced about seven months after I became CEO last year.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: There are a lot of lawsuits regarding this situation. Is there-- do you see an insight to them being settled in one fell swoop?', "ALAN SHAW: You know, I'm leaving that up to our legal team. There are a number of lawsuits, and I really can't comment on that. What I can tell you is we're going to continue to get better coming out of this. We're going to be a stronger company. We're advancing safety. We're advancing service. I'm really proud of the way that we've responded to this.", 'The entire organization has become aligned around our new strategy, our new vision and our response in East Palestine.', 'BRIAN SOZZI: Is it right that the total cost so far is-- I think it was it $966 million? Is that--', "ALAN SHAW: Yeah, we've estimated around $900 million so far. Now there could be additional lawsuits, there could be additional fines, there could also be insurance settlements. In fact, we've already started to pull those in. And there could be third party claims as well.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: So for an investor looking to put money to work in Norfolk Southern, is that-- should they expect a similar number? I imagine this weighs on the finances of the company. Is that number similar-- that might pop up next year in terms of total cost?', "ALAN SHAW: You know, much of that cost has been the environmental remediation. As I noted, we've exited the most intense phase of that but there are other things that could come up with lawsuits or fines but again, the insurance settlements as well.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: A lot of focus so far at the conference on the state of the economy. Heard Hans Vestberg, chairman and CEO of Verizon, talk about the consumer is doing well, the lodging industry, Marriott CEO, Anthony Capuano talking about that doing well but maybe just a little bit of a slowdown. The rail industry is in a down cycle. Why?', 'ALAN SHAW: What industry did you say?', 'BRIAN SOZZI: The rail industry.', "ALAN SHAW: You know, what we're seeing is a really weak truck market, overcapacity in trucking, and so there's been kind of a Great Recession in the truck market for about 22 months. There's some indication that that's ending, right? Spot markets are no longer on the decline as I talk to customers. We're seeing inventory destocking come to an end.", "And as-- we serve 5,000 customers so we've got this really unique view of the US economy. We touch about every market. And as I look around, you're starting to see this consumer do fairly well as you noted. I believe we're in a manufacturing supercycle. We've seen investment in new factory builds triple and so far in 2023 relative to they were-- the run rate they were in the previous decade, and it's really in our service region, it's in the Midwest, and it's in the Southeast.", "And I was talking to the CEO of a European automaker, and he was talking about how if he wants to sell production in the United States, he needs to produce in the United States, and there's a lot of advantages for onshoring and-- in the United States and it's cheap and reliable electricity, it's a logistics infrastructure that's already in place, and it's a talented workforce and that really plays to the strengths of our strategy going forward, which is to use service to drive top tier revenue growth and industry competitive margins.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Important distinction there. So you're saying rail has been in a down cycle, but that's not the same as a recession?", "ALAN SHAW: No, I don't-- I don't believe we're in a recession. I think we're in a-- we've been in a freight recession, because there's been overcapacity in the truck market and that's our primary form of competition. Now we've got the most powerful intermodal franchise in the East, and so it's only a matter of time when that recovers.", "And when the US consumer does recover and the truck market recovers, we're going to be coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: Have you had to furlough any workers?', "ALAN SHAW: No, we continue to hire, right. We're building for the long-term at Norfolk Southern. We're investing in our future and we're investing in locomotives and intermodal facilities and freight cars that help us compete with truck and technology and safety and our people as well. That's been my commitment. And day one that I became CEO about 18 months ago, I was out in the field, and I was visiting with our crews in the crew rooms and in the locomotive cabs, because I wanted to express my deep appreciation and respect for what they do for Norfolk Southern, for our customers and for the US economy.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Well, it's like you're still-- you work your whole life, Alan-- and I think a lot of people watching this can relate and a lot of probably a lot of people in this room. You work your whole life to get to this top spot and within 18 months, you're dealing with a major crisis. What has that like been-- been that for you personally? What has that been like?", "ALAN SHAW: As you-- the first day you sit in the seat, you understand it's about accountability, right, and I just knew that each and every day, we were going to do the next right thing. I was going to follow our North Star. I was going to follow our values, focus on the long-term, and my goal for my team is-- was that 5 years from now, 10 years from now, when we look back on this, we can have a response that makes us proud and a response that makes the folks in East Palestine proud.", "At the same time, we're implementing this unique vision, a better way forward in the rail industry. Look, if you think about rail, rail is seated sharing to truck for the last 25 years despite being lower cost, a higher safety, better much-- better safety metrics, better sustainability with respect to the carbon footprint, and it's because rail hasn't delivered consistently a good service product.", "And so when I became CEO about 18 months ago, we went on a hiring spree. We started hiring conductors. We're investing in the future and we're investing in service, because I've got so much confidence in the unique strengths of our franchise and our customers and our employees that I know that we can deliver that top tier revenue growth with industry competitive margins. That's what's going to drive long-term shareholder value for Norfolk Southern.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Lastly, Alan, we're about 15 seconds left. Throughout this crisis period, as a leader, how have you stayed centered? These have to be incredibly challenging periods.", "ALAN SHAW: I've got a lot of confidence that I know we're doing the right thing and so that allows you to block out a lot of-- a lot of the noise and focus on the mission. And when you get up every day, you just say each and every day, I'm going to do the next right thing, and I'm going to see this thing through.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Well, I look forward to continuing to track this progress. Norfolk Southern CEO, Alan Shaw. Thanks for coming down, and really, it's good to see you again. We appreciate it.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah, it's a pleasure, Brian. Thank you so much.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: Appreciate it.']

Title: With 75% ownership, Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE:NSC) boasts of strong institutional backing
Text: ["Institutions' substantial holdings in Norfolk Southern implies that they have significant influence over the company's share price", 'The top 24 shareholders own 51% of the company', 'Using data from analyst forecasts alongside ownership research, one can better assess the future performance of a company', 'Every investor in Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE:NSC) should be aware of the most powerful shareholder groups. The group holding the most number of shares in the company, around 75% to be precise, is institutions. That is, the group stands to benefit the most if the stock rises (or lose the most if there is a downturn).', 'Since institutional have access to huge amounts of capital, their market moves tend to receive a lot of scrutiny by retail or individual investors. Hence, having a considerable amount of institutional money invested in a company is often regarded as a desirable trait.', "Let's delve deeper into each type of owner of Norfolk Southern, beginning with the chart below.", ' Check out our latest analysis for Norfolk Southern ', 'Many institutions measure their performance against an index that approximates the local market. So they usually pay more attention to companies that are included in major indices.', "As you can see, institutional investors have a fair amount of stake in Norfolk Southern. This implies the analysts working for those institutions have looked at the stock and they like it. But just like anyone else, they could be wrong. If multiple institutions change their view on a stock at the same time, you could see the share price drop fast. It's therefore worth looking at Norfolk Southern's earnings history below. Of course, the future is what really matters.", "Institutional investors own over 50% of the company, so together than can probably strongly influence board decisions. Norfolk Southern is not owned by hedge funds. The Vanguard Group, Inc. is currently the company's largest shareholder with 8.2% of shares outstanding. Meanwhile, the second and third largest shareholders, hold 6.8% and 4.7%, of the shares outstanding, respectively.", 'After doing some more digging, we found that the top 24 have the combined ownership of 51% in the company, suggesting that no single shareholder has significant control over the company.', "Researching institutional ownership is a good way to gauge and filter a stock's expected performance. The same can be achieved by studying analyst sentiments. Quite a few analysts cover the stock, so you could look into forecast growth quite easily.", 'The definition of company insiders can be subjective and does vary between jurisdictions. Our data reflects individual insiders, capturing board members at the very least. Company management run the business, but the CEO will answer to the board, even if he or she is a member of it.', 'Insider ownership is positive when it signals leadership are thinking like the true owners of the company. However, high insider ownership can also give immense power to a small group within the company. This can be negative in some circumstances.', 'Our information suggests that Norfolk Southern Corporation insiders own under 1% of the company. Title: 3 Dividend Stocks with Strong Growth Potential in Q4
Text: ['If this is the beginning of a broader market rally, many short-term investors may shift away from dividend stocks. After a year or more of playing defense, it makes\xa0sense that risk-tolerant traders and investors will want to consider equities with more upside. ', 'But, there’s still a case for solid dividend stocks in your portfolio. These companies aren’t going to be on anyone’s high-growth stock list, but many of these stocks still offer annual earnings growth that outpaces the interest rates offered by long-term Treasury bills. For mature companies that means robust cash flow, which in turn means dividend increases. ', 'Earnings growth is also one of the best predictors of future stock price gains. Many of these stocks are trading at attractive valuations that give them plenty of upside heading into 2024. ', 'InvestorPlace - Stock Market News, Stock Advice & Trading Tips', 'And several of these companies are in line to raise their dividends during the next round of earnings. Here are three evergreen dividend stocks to buy for growth as well as income. ', 'Source: IgorGolovniov / Shutterstock', 'Constellation Brands (NYSE:STZ) falls in the consumer discretionary sector. This is a sector that’s fallen out of favor with investors as consumers tighten their belts and trim their budgets.', 'But it’s also a sin stock. And sin stocks tend to perform well in bull or bear markets. In fact, the defensive nature of these companies leads to consistent demand regardless of the health of the economy, even during recessions. ', 'Specific to Constellation Brands, the company generates five times the sales per SKU of the two other top beer suppliers. And Constellation is home to two of the most popular beer brands in Modelo and Corona.', 'Despite a solid earnings report in early October, STZ stock is still well off its 52-week high and is down 10% in the last three months. However, with projections of 12% earnings growth in the next 12 months, there’s good reason to believe the stock may have found a base of support around $230. Plus, Constellation has been aggressively increasing its dividend in the last two years. And sometime early next year, investors are likely to be rewarded with a dividend increase. ', 'Source: IgorGolovniov / Shutterstock.com', 'Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO) is another dividend stock that offers investors a compelling combination of growth and value. Coke isn’t a stock typically associated with strong growth. As evidence of that, KO stock is up only 13% in the past five years. ', 'However, KO stock is up 7% in the last month despite the broader market being under pressure. This is likely a response to a broader sell-off in the stock on concerns about multiple threats including inflation and weight loss drugs.', 'But a strong earnings report should put those concerns to bed. And with the stock still down 10% in 2023, there’s room for Coke’s stock to move higher. Especially when the company guided higher for both revenue and earnings. ', 'Plus, long-time dividend investors in KO stock know that the Dividend King is ready for another dividend increase. The last dividend increase was approximately 5% on earnings growth of 7%. That suggests there may be an even higher dividend increase in store for KO shareholders. ', 'Source: Shutterstock', 'Like many transportation stocks, Norfolk Southern (NYSE:NSC) has been beaten down this year. NSC stock is down 21% in 2023. However, in the last month, the railroad delivered a piece of good news by announcing it had completed the “intensive” part of its environmental remediation efforts in East Palestine. The company has already committed over $96.5 million to the affected area. ', 'That will allow investors to focus on what will likely be an upcoming dividend increase. Forecasts are for the company to grow earnings by 9% in the next 12 months. That’s in line with the 11-cent per share increase shareholders received last year. Title: Cincinnati voters approve sale of city-owned railroad to Norfolk Southern
Text: ['Cincinnati voters decided on Election Day to allow their city to sell the Cincinnati Southern Railway to Norfolk Southern.', 'Tuesday’s vote was 51.56% in favor of the sale and 48.44% against the sale, according to Ballotpedia. By votes, those supporting the sale were 43,173 and those against the sale were 40,559 — a difference of 2,614.', 'The Cincinnati Southern Railway Board of Trustees owns the 382-mile railroad in a trust and leases it to NS (NYSE: NSC) for Cincinnati’s benefit. The city currently receives about $25 million annually from NS, according to a local news report in February.', 'The city announced in November 2022 that it was considering selling the railway to NS for $1.62 billion to help fund city infrastructure improvements, according to news reports. NS would pay for the transaction through a combination of internal and external sources, the railroad said last year.', 'Cincinnati has owned the land beneath the track for almost two centuries, but NS operates the rail line, according to NS.', 'In response to Tuesday’s note, NS spokesperson Tom Crosson said: “This is a victory for the citizens of Cincinnati. Current and future generations will reap the benefits of new infrastructure investments, helping to create a better future for the city. We appreciate all of the community leaders and groups who endorsed Issue 22 — especially Mayor Aftab Pureval, the City Council, and the Board of Trustees of the Cincinnati Southern Railway. We also thank the staff and volunteers who made this a successful campaign. Now, we will work with the city to finalize the sale, which we expect to close in Q1 of 2024.”', 'Subscribe to FreightWaves’ e-newsletters and get the latest insights on freight right in your inbox.', 'Click here for more FreightWaves articles by Joanna Marsh.', 'Cincinnati voters to decide on sale of Cincinnati Southern Railway to NS', 'Norfolk Southern wants close look at proposed CPKC-CSX Southeast corridor', 'Norfolk Southern says higher costs will pay off in long term', 'The post Cincinnati voters approve sale of city-owned railroad to Norfolk Southern appeared first on FreightWaves.']

Title: Norfolk Southern CEO: we're in a 'manufacturing super-cycle'
Text: ['"We\'ve got the most powerful automotive franchise in the east, and so it\'s only a matter of time when that recovers", says Alan Shaw, President and CEO of Norfolk Southern (NSC). He spoke with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi about the current downturn in the rail industry. Shaw attributed the decline to broader economic factors, like the freight recession in the trucking market, which has suppressed spot market rates and inventory restocking.', 'Despite these headwinds, Shaw expressed confidence that the rail industry is entering a "manufacturing super-cycle."', 'When the U.S. consumer and the truck market recovers, we\'re gonna be "coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals", Shaw told Yahoo Finance.', 'Click here to watch more from Yahoo Finance Invest.', 'BRIAN SOZZI: A lot of focus so far at the conference on the state of the economy, heard Hans Vestberg, the chairman and CEO of Verizon talked about the consumer is doing well, the lodging industry, Marriott CEO, Anthony Capuano talking about that doing well but maybe just a little bit of a slowdown. The rail industry is in a down cycle. Why?', 'ALAN SHAW: What industry did you say?', 'BRIAN SOZZI: The rail industry is--', "ALAN SHAW: You know, what we're seeing is a really weak truck market, overcapacity in trucking, and so there's been kind of a freight recession in the truck market for about 22 months. There's some indication that that's ending, right? Spot markets are no longer on the decline. As I talk to customers, we're seeing inventory destocking come to an end. And as-- we serve 5,000 customers so we've got this really unique view of the US economy. We touch about every market.", "And as I look around, you're starting to see this consumer do fairly well as you noted, I believe we're in a manufacturing supercycle. We've seen investment in new factory builds triple and-- so far in 2023 relative to they were-- the run rate they were in the previous decade, and it's really in our service region, it's in the Midwest, and it's in the Southeast.", "And I was talking to the CEO of a European automaker and he was talking about how if he wants to sell production in the United States, he needs to produce in the United States and there's a lot of advantages for onshoring and-- in the United States and it's cheap and reliable electricity, it's a logistics infrastructure that's already in place, and it's a talented workforce and that really plays to the strengths of our strategy going forward, which is to use service to drive top tier revenue growth and industry competitive margins.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Important distinction there. So you're saying rail has been in a down cycle, but that's not the same as a recession?", "ALAN SHAW: No, I don't-- I don't believe we're in a recession. I think we're in a-- we've been in a freight recession, because there's been overcapacity in the truck market and that's our primary form of competition. Now we've got the most powerful intermodal franchise in the East, and so it's only a matter of time when that recovers and when the US consumer does recover and the truck market can-- recovers, we're going to be coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals."]

Title: How Norfolk Southern is changing after train derailment
Text: ["Norfolk Southern (NSC) has been under a microscope ever since the major chemical spill in East Palestine, Ohio. The company has taken major steps toward addressing safety concerns, including new training programs. Alan Shaw, Norfolk Southern CEO and President, sits down with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to discuss the company's progress with the ongoing cleanup in East Palestine as well as the strides the company is making in safety.", 'Shaw explains efforts made to improve safety. "We have... a machine visioning train inspection portal, which is basically a shed that goes around the tracks, train goes through track speed about 60 miles an hour. It\'s got 38 cameras that take about a thousand pictures of each rail car and immediately uses AI to spot potential safety defects...What we are focused on at Norfolk Southern is enhancing safety and enhancing service and really competing in that $860 billion dollar truck and logistics market."', 'Click here to watch more from Yahoo Finance Invest.', "BRIAN SOZZI: I know it's been an incredibly busy time for your company, and I was thinking back like, how do you prepare for a segment like this? And I think it starts with understanding you as a human, as a leader. Of course, the train derailments are very much covered throughout news in East Palestine. Take us through how you were raised, your family upbringing, and-- because I think that tells a lot on how you respond to the situation.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah. I was-- my father was in Vietnam. He's a Marine Lieutenant, did two tours, and I was raised, for a number of years, by my grandmother, my aunt and my mom. Three really strong willed women. And my grandmother worked as an assistant in the financial aid office and put four kids through college, right.", "And she paid it forward, and she kept her promises, and that's one of the things I learned is trust, accountability and keeping your promises, and that's kind of the North Star and that's what we followed as we went through this crisis is we said we were going to make it right, we said we were going to do the right things, and each and every day we've kept our promises.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: When you get that call that a train derailed in East Palestine, toxic chemicals going into the air, who is Alan Shaw one minute after that call?', "ALAN SHAW: Oh, I'm thinking about the community. I'm thinking about the safety of our crews. I'm thinking about the safety of the first responders. Your immediate question is, any injuries, any deaths, any hazmat releases, and we're really fortunate that there were no injuries or deaths. I pulled the team together immediately afterwards, and I said, look, we're going to make this right. We're going to do the right thing.", "And I didn't know what that meant, right. I've never been to East Palace, and it's a wonderful community of about 4,700 people, but what I knew is I had to listen, I had to learn, I had to act with humility, and I had to take decisive action. And so I would go to the community. I've been there multiple times a month. I was just-- I was there just last week and you engage with the community and you go into listening sessions and you go into the churches and in the schools and in the family rooms and into the businesses and you ask them, what can Norfolk Southern do to help?", "I knew that we would bring Norfolk Southern's resources-- we're a strong company-- to bear and the community would direct where we'd go. And so we've already committed over $100 million to helping the community recover and helping the community thrive, and there's more work to be done.", "BRIAN SOZZI: As a leader, public company forward or the face of the company in many respects, what is it like to take that criticism that you've gotten even despite all the efforts you've been trying to put forth on the ground?", "ALAN SHAW: We're a safe railroad, and I knew that. Last year, the number of derailments on Norfolk Southern was the lowest in two decades. But I know we can get better. And as I looked through this crisis-- a crisis is an opportunity to really kind of like test your leadership and your resolve, it also is an opportunity to accelerate change.", 'And I knew that coming out of this, we were going to be a stronger company. And so one of the things I did is I looked outside the rail industry for inspiration. I used to work at Newport News Shipbuilding in the nuclear department installing nuclear reactors and aircraft carriers, and so I had a really good idea--', "BRIAN SOZZI: That's a pressure cooker.", "ALAN SHAW: Yeah. I had a really good idea of the safety culture of the Admiral Rickover's nuclear Navy, and so I reached out to a former Admiral who used to run the Navy nuclear propulsion system and asked him to put together a team of former Navy nukes reporting directly to me as an independent consultant and help us with our safety culture. And they've been on the ground for about six months.", "They're going to be here two to three years. They're engaging with our employees, our craft colleagues, and they're going to make us a safer railroad. We're going to be the gold standard of safety.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: So three years from now, how do you-- how is Norfolk a safer railroad?', "ALAN SHAW: Well, we're going to continue to invest in our infrastructure. We invest over $1 billion in safety every year. We're going to continue to train our employees. We're going to use technology. We have partnered with the Georgia Tech Research Institute on a machine visioning train inspection portal, which is basically a shed that goes around the tracks.", "The train goes through it, track speed about 60 miles an hour. It's got 38 cameras that take about 1,000 pictures of each rail car and immediately uses AI to spot potential safety defects. And that's something that I know that a conductor in Chicago at night in February just won't catch with the human eye. We are using technology and automated intelligence to enhance our safety.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: What are some of the specifics that Norfolk is doing on the ground in East Palestine? And how are you putting the capital to work to rebuild the community?', "ALAN SHAW: So a number of things. We just achieved a pretty significant milestone just about a week or two ago as we exited the most intense phase of the environmental remediation. Brian, we moved 170,000 tons of contaminated soil off site to EPA approved landfills, which were specifically designed to handle that. We've moved 36 million gallons of contaminated water off site. So that's a big move for the community.", "We've announced a $20 million park improvement project. One of the first times I was there, I met with some community leaders in someone's basement, and they talked to me a lot about the park, and so I went to the park. It's an 81 acre facility in the middle of the community that's a source of pride for them, and they asked me if I could help them improve it, and so I brought Norfolk Southern's resources to bear.", "I was just at a groundbreaking ceremony a couple of weeks ago for a regional first responder training facility. We're committing $20 million to that, and that really-- that's important to me personally, because I wanted to express my appreciation for the first responders from Ohio and Pennsylvania and West Virginia who rushed to the scene. They're the heroes here. And first responders are folks who devote their entire career to protecting the communities we serve.", "BRIAN SOZZI: What do you think when you hear politicians say railroads are not safe, they're just trying to jack up their profits by taking away safety standards?", "ALAN SHAW: Well, railroads are clearly the safest form of transportation across land, we're also the most efficient. Now what we're focused on, on Norfolk Southern is enhancing safety and enhancing service and really competing in that $860 billion truck and logistics market, you know. We want to have top tier revenue growth in the industry with industry competitive margins, that's the strategy that we announced about seven months after I became CEO last year.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: There are a lot of lawsuits regarding this situation. Is there-- do you see an insight to them being settled in one fell swoop?', "ALAN SHAW: You know, I'm leaving that up to our legal team. There are a number of lawsuits, and I really can't comment on that. What I can tell you is we're going to continue to get better coming out of this. We're going to be a stronger company. We're advancing safety. We're advancing service. I'm really proud of the way that we've responded to this.", 'The entire organization has become aligned around our new strategy, our new vision and our response in East Palestine.', 'BRIAN SOZZI: Is it right that the total cost so far is-- I think it was it $966 million? Is that--', "ALAN SHAW: Yeah, we've estimated around $900 million so far. Now there could be additional lawsuits, there could be additional fines, there could also be insurance settlements. In fact, we've already started to pull those in. And there could be third party claims as well.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: So for an investor looking to put money to work in Norfolk Southern, is that-- should they expect a similar number? I imagine this weighs on the finances of the company. Is that number similar-- that might pop up next year in terms of total cost?', "ALAN SHAW: You know, much of that cost has been the environmental remediation. As I noted, we've exited the most intense phase of that but there are other things that could come up with lawsuits or fines but again, the insurance settlements as well.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: A lot of focus so far at the conference on the state of the economy. Heard Hans Vestberg, chairman and CEO of Verizon, talk about the consumer is doing well, the lodging industry, Marriott CEO, Anthony Capuano talking about that doing well but maybe just a little bit of a slowdown. The rail industry is in a down cycle. Why?', 'ALAN SHAW: What industry did you say?', 'BRIAN SOZZI: The rail industry.', "ALAN SHAW: You know, what we're seeing is a really weak truck market, overcapacity in trucking, and so there's been kind of a Great Recession in the truck market for about 22 months. There's some indication that that's ending, right? Spot markets are no longer on the decline as I talk to customers. We're seeing inventory destocking come to an end.", "And as-- we serve 5,000 customers so we've got this really unique view of the US economy. We touch about every market. And as I look around, you're starting to see this consumer do fairly well as you noted. I believe we're in a manufacturing supercycle. We've seen investment in new factory builds triple and so far in 2023 relative to they were-- the run rate they were in the previous decade, and it's really in our service region, it's in the Midwest, and it's in the Southeast.", "And I was talking to the CEO of a European automaker, and he was talking about how if he wants to sell production in the United States, he needs to produce in the United States, and there's a lot of advantages for onshoring and-- in the United States and it's cheap and reliable electricity, it's a logistics infrastructure that's already in place, and it's a talented workforce and that really plays to the strengths of our strategy going forward, which is to use service to drive top tier revenue growth and industry competitive margins.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Important distinction there. So you're saying rail has been in a down cycle, but that's not the same as a recession?", "ALAN SHAW: No, I don't-- I don't believe we're in a recession. I think we're in a-- we've been in a freight recession, because there's been overcapacity in the truck market and that's our primary form of competition. Now we've got the most powerful intermodal franchise in the East, and so it's only a matter of time when that recovers.", "And when the US consumer does recover and the truck market recovers, we're going to be coiled up and poised for growth with high incrementals.", 'BRIAN SOZZI: Have you had to furlough any workers?', "ALAN SHAW: No, we continue to hire, right. We're building for the long-term at Norfolk Southern. We're investing in our future and we're investing in locomotives and intermodal facilities and freight cars that help us compete with truck and technology and safety and our people as well. That's been my commitment. And day one that I became CEO about 18 months ago, I was out in the field, and I was visiting with our crews in the crew rooms and in the locomotive cabs, because I wanted to express my deep appreciation and respect for what they do for Norfolk Southern, for our customers and for the US economy.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Well, it's like you're still-- you work your whole life, Alan-- and I think a lot of people watching this can relate and a lot of probably a lot of people in this room. You work your whole life to get to this top spot and within 18 months, you're dealing with a major crisis. What has that like been-- been that for you personally? What has that been like?", "ALAN SHAW: As you-- the first day you sit in the seat, you understand it's about accountability, right, and I just knew that each and every day, we were going to do the next right thing. I was going to follow our North Star. I was going to follow our values, focus on the long-term, and my goal for my team is-- was that 5 years from now, 10 years from now, when we look back on this, we can have a response that makes us proud and a response that makes the folks in East Palestine proud.", "At the same time, we're implementing this unique vision, a better way forward in the rail industry. Look, if you think about rail, rail is seated sharing to truck for the last 25 years despite being lower cost, a higher safety, better much-- better safety metrics, better sustainability with respect to the carbon footprint, and it's because rail hasn't delivered consistently a good service product.", "And so when I became CEO about 18 months ago, we went on a hiring spree. We started hiring conductors. We're investing in the future and we're investing in service, because I've got so much confidence in the unique strengths of our franchise and our customers and our employees that I know that we can deliver that top tier revenue growth with industry competitive margins. That's what's going to drive long-term shareholder value for Norfolk Southern.", "BRIAN SOZZI: Lastly, Alan, we're about 15 seconds left. Title: 3 Dividend Stocks with Strong Growth Potential in Q4
Text: ['If this is the beginning of a broader market rally, many short-term investors may shift away from dividend stocks. Title: Cincinnati voters approve sale of city-owned railroad to Norfolk Southern
Text: ['Cincinnati voters decided on Election Day to allow their city to sell the Cincinnati Southern Railway to Norfolk Southern.', 'Tuesday’s vote was 51.56% in favor of the sale and 48.44% against the sale, according to Ballotpedia. By votes, those supporting the sale were 43,173 and those against the sale were 40,559 — a difference of 2,614.', 'The Cincinnati Southern Railway Board of Trustees owns the 382-mile railroad in a trust and leases it to NS (NYSE: NSC) for Cincinnati’s benefit. The city currently receives about $25 million annually from NS, according to a local news report in February.', 'The city announced in November 2022 that it was considering selling the railway to NS for $1.62 billion to help fund city infrastructure improvements, according to news reports. NS would pay for the transaction through a combination of internal and external sources, the railroad said last year.', 'Cincinnati has owned the land beneath the track for almost two centuries, but NS operates the rail line, according to NS.', 'In response to Tuesday’s note, NS spokesperson Tom Crosson said: “This is a victory for the citizens of Cincinnati. Current and future generations will reap the benefits of new infrastructure investments, helping to create a better future for the city. We appreciate all of the community leaders and groups who endorsed Issue 22 — especially Mayor Aftab Pureval, the City Council, and the Board of Trustees of the Cincinnati Southern Railway. We also thank the staff and volunteers who made this a successful campaign. Now, we will work with the city to finalize the sale, which we expect to close in Q1 of 2024.”', 'Subscribe to FreightWaves’ e-newsletters and get the latest insights on freight right in your inbox.', 'Click here for more FreightWaves articles by Joanna Marsh.', 'Cincinnati voters to decide on sale of Cincinnati Southern Railway to NS', 'Norfolk Southern wants close look at proposed CPKC-CSX Southeast corridor', 'Norfolk Southern says higher costs will pay off in long term', 'The post Cincinnati voters approve sale of city-owned railroad to Norfolk Southern appeared first on FreightWaves.']
